metadata.name: Dutch Commercial Republicanism
metadata.description: The seventeenth-century Dutch commercial republican tradition associated with the De la Courts and the regent defence of provincial liberty, commerce and toleration against dynastic rule. It differs from modern neoconservatism.
metadata.period: Dutch commercial and regent republican thought, 1650–1672
metadata.scope: The commercial republican strand expressed in Interest van Holland and the defence of true freedom, checked against scholarship on regent and provincial institutions. It is not every faction in the Dutch Republic, a modern democratic franchise, or a claim that colonial practice fulfilled the doctrine.
metadata.phrase: A society of self-governing provinces and towns where secure civil institutions, freedom of commerce and toleration support prosperity without dynastic domination.
